description: Canonical, machine-readable readiness vocabulary for the Aether platform. Single source of truth for every readiness/capability token used by the certification plane (Python), the persisted capability lifecycle, and the presentation plane (TypeScript). Neither bound file is generated — both stay hand-written for ergonomics — but scripts/validate_readiness_vocabulary.py fails CI whenever the Python enum, the TypeScript union, this file, or packages/shared/contracts/evidence-manifest.schema.json disagree on membership, rank ordering, or the production_ready-is-never-inferred rule. v2 replaces the v1 draft whose PRODUCTION_READY / NOT_IN_RELEASE / EXTERNALLY_BLOCKED / MOCKED_LOCAL / IMPLEMENTED / CONFIGURED Python members never existed: production_ready is a claim DIMENSION (never an enum state), release-plan classifications are their own category, and the retired draft progression tokens survive only as aliases.

rules.singleSource: No component may define a readiness token that is absent from this file, and no token here may lack a binding to at least one consumer (Python enum member or TypeScript union literal). A token with neither is dead vocabulary and must be deleted.
rules.rankScale: Certification ranks are spaced by 10 so future intermediate states can be inserted without renumbering. Only relative order is contractual; no consumer may depend on the absolute integers.
rules.offRampBelowProgression: Every certification token with progression=false must rank strictly below every token with progression=true, so that a `readiness_rank(x) >= readiness_rank(CREDENTIAL_WAITING)` gate can never admit an off-ramp state.
rules.inferableIsExhaustive: The set of certification tokens with inferable=true must equal EXACTLY the set of tokens that ReadinessDimensions._coarse_state can return. Adding a return to that function without flipping the flag here fails the validator, and vice versa.
rules.productionReadyNeverInferred: production_ready is a claim DIMENSION on ReadinessDimensions, never a CredentialReadiness enum member and never a certification-ladder state. The honesty validator refuses production_ready=true without live_validated AND security_reviewed (AND externally_audited when requires_external_audit). The validator asserts no enum member or certification token named production_ready exists.
rules.presentationIsNotCertification: Tokens in category=presentation describe the freshness/health of a rendered read (stale, partial, error, connection_testing, entitlement and credential-entry states). They never appear in the certification ladder, carry rank=null, and must never be written into a certification record or an evidence manifest.
rules.releasePlanIsNotRuntime: Tokens in category=release_plan classify a capability's place in a release (per config/capability_matrix.yaml profile states). They are not runtime readiness states, carry rank=null, and have no Python enum binding.
rules.aliasUniqueness: An alias must not collide with any token id or with any other token's alias. Aliases exist so a mandated release-plan spelling can resolve onto the token the running code already serialises.
rules.releasePlanCoverage: Every token in releasePlanVocabulary must resolve to exactly one token id or alias in this file.

production_ready.rule: Requires live_validated AND security_reviewed; additionally externally_audited when requires_external_audit is set. Structure never infers it (_coarse_state cannot return it; derive() never sets it).

tokens.description: Pulled from release: turned off on purpose by an operator, a compliance hold, or a deprecation. The most severe off-ramp state.
Credentials were revoked (by the tenant, the provider, or an operator). Requires credential resubmission and re-certification.
Reversibly stopped by an operator action or a kill switch. Resuming restores the previously certified level without re-certification.

Previously working, now regressed: a dependency or repeated health probe failed. Auto-recoverable. An off-ramp state ranked below the progression so it can never satisfy an at-least-credential-waiting gate.
Descriptor only: decode and execution paths are not implemented. The forbidden-for-first-release marker.
Everything Aether controls is done (code-complete + infra-defined); the capability is waiting on a credential to be issued, accepted, or propagated. The honest ceiling for a credentialless release.
Verified end to end against recorded/replayed provider traffic. Proves decode and mapping correctness; proves nothing about the live provider.

An active credential version exists for the (tenant, provider, environment, capability) coordinate but has not yet passed a connection test. Rotation demotes a certified capability back here bound to the new credential version.
The supplied credential passed a real connection/identity test (signature self-check, live probe, chain-identity check, or signer-ownership check as the slot declares).

Verified end to end in the provider's sandbox with real credentials. Still not production: sandbox data, sandbox limits, sandbox failure modes. For a credential-gated capability this implies connection_validated.

Executing against the production provider with production credentials. The highest state reachable by inference from evidence. A production_ready CLAIM additionally requires security review (and external audit where required) — see claimDimensions.

Deliberately omitted by product or release policy for this release class (a capability-matrix profile state). Distinct from the runtime DISABLED off-ramp: nothing regressed — the capability was never offered here.

Deliberately out of scope for the current release. The capability may exist in the tree but is not shipped, not certified, and not counted by the readiness scorecard. A capability-matrix profile state, not a runtime readiness state.

Progress is blocked by a third party Aether does not control — partner onboarding, regulator sign-off, or an unfulfilled provider agreement. Distinct from credential_waiting, where the credential path is open and only propagation is pending.
The tenant's plan or entitlement does not include this capability. A billing fact, not a build state.
No credentials or configuration have been supplied for this tenant yet.
Configuration is present but provider credentials are still needed from the tenant. Requires user action.
The provider rejected the supplied credentials.
A connection probe against the provider is in flight. Transient.
Provider resources are actively being created. Transient.
Runtime capability truth could not be established for this read.
Presentation spelling of a fully live capability; partner_live is the certification token. Never a certification state.
Data is present but older than its freshness SLA.
Some expected inputs are present, not all.
The capability read failed.
The capability is halted by an active kill switch (presentation of a SUSPENDED certification state driven by a kill switch).
